name: Zapatismo
summary: Zapatismo (neozapatismo) is the outlook of the EZLN and its Chiapas support bases: indigenous autonomy and land, democracy understood as governing by obeying, and opposition to neoliberal capitalism. It refuses to seize state power, builds self-governing communities from below, and blends Maya tradition, liberation theology, anarchist and Marxist elements.
scope: The mainstream neozapatista outlook from the First Declaration of the Lacandon Jungle (1993) through the Sixth Declaration (2005) and the autonomous municipalities and Good Government Councils. It excludes the pre-1994 Marxist guerrilla origins in detail, Emiliano Zapata's historical agrarianism, and later organizational changes after 2023. Many statements outside its documented concerns are inferred and marked low confidence.

sources.usedFor: Good Government assemblies, governing by obeying, consultas, separation of EZLN military from civil authorities.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Health care is among the First Declaration's listed demands and the autonomous municipalities run their own health systems, so adherents want it guaranteed for all, though through community rather than state provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the Sixth Declaration's call for a program of struggle covering work and from its anti-exploitation stance; wage policy is not specifically addressed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Sixth Declaration calls neoliberal globalization a war of conquest and capitalism a system based on exploitation, so the claim that free markets allocate better is rejected.

public-ownership.rationale: The Sixth Declaration opposes privatizing electricity, oil and water, but Zapatistas favor community and collective control over state ownership, so the answer is split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from anti-capitalist and redistributive aims of the national program of struggle of the left.

unions-good.rationale: The Sixth Declaration seeks alliance with workers' organizations and the exploited, but unions are not a main Zapatista subject, so this is inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: The EZLN centres communal land and opposes the 1992 end of land redistribution; private property is not treated as an overriding right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Opposition to neoliberal corporate power implies support for curbing corporations, though Zapatistas distrust the state as regulator.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from demands for food, health and housing; Zapatistas reject government handouts as co-optation but not provision of basic needs.

worker-ownership.rationale: Autonomous production is collective and the Sixth Declaration attacks exploitation of workers; collective ownership by producers fits, though workplaces are not the focus.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to the bad government and its political police, whom the First Declaration accuses of abuses.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Zapatista territory prohibits drug planting and use, so adherents oppose legalization in their own communities.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; adherents stress respect and dignity but there is no documented position on legal speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: The principle of governing by obeying and rotation of leaders ("not to change masters every six years") rejects strongman rule.

state-harmful.rationale: The EZLN says it does not seek state power and rejects the bad government, yet demands a new constitution and democratic government; scholars dispute whether it is anarchist.

limit-guns.rationale: The EZLN is itself armed, but advocates civil and peaceful struggle now; no stated position on civilian gun law.

empower-police-military.rationale: The First Declaration calls the federal army the pillar of the dictatorship, and the movement demands the military be subordinate to civilian authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the Women's Revolutionary Law's emphasis on women's dignity and the movement's ban on alcohol and drugs; sex work is not directly addressed.

decide-locally.rationale: The Sixth Declaration says peoples themselves decide who governs and how, and autonomous municipalities with assemblies are the core of the model.

rehabilitation.rationale: Autonomous justice relies on community mediation and labor rather than prisons, implying rehabilitative aims, though the sources do not state it.

traditional-family.rationale: Zapatistas uphold community life but their women's law challenges patriarchal family norms, so adherents do not treat the traditional family as foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: No source I opened states a position and communities are mixed, so adherents are split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the sources I opened; adherents in Maya communities are divided.

more-religion-public.rationale: The EZLN rejects ties to any religious authority despite liberation-theology influence; inferred opposition to more religion in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement arose to end 500 years of exclusion of indigenous peoples and demands indigenous rights and dignity.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Women's equality is central but no source states a view on whether gender is a social construct.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Zapatistas defend indigenous cultures; whether this equals national culture is unclear, so adherents are split.

gradual-change.rationale: They launched an armed uprising and demand deep change, yet later pursue slow autonomy building; they do not defer to established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Sixth Declaration calls for solidarity with the dispossessed everywhere and rejects borders as tools of capital; stance inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The EZLN condemns institutions of neoliberal globalization and relies on grassroots international solidarity rather than the UN.

free-trade.rationale: The uprising began on the day NAFTA took effect and the EZLN condemns neoliberal free trade as worsening inequality.

nation-first.rationale: The Sixth Declaration stresses international solidarity of the exploited over national interest, though it defends Mexican resources against privatization.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialist rejection of Western war; not addressed directly.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from the internationalism of the Sixth Declaration and its solidarity with migrants and the dispossessed.

limit-growth.rationale: Opposition to mega-infrastructure and defense of land, forests and water implies limits on extractive growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Strong environmental rhetoric, but climate policy is not addressed; adherents would back drastic change if led from below.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Zapatistas use technology tactically but see the problem as capitalism, not lack of technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from environmental opposition to destructive megaprojects.

revolution-justified.rationale: The First Declaration invoked the right to alter government by arms, though the Sixth Declaration shifts to peaceful struggle for now.

experts-over-public.rationale: Decisions go to community assemblies and delegates obey the people, so expert rule is rejected.

central-planning.rationale: The movement builds from below and rejects top-down command; it also opposes capitalism, but not through central plans.

socialized-markets.rationale: Zapatista cooperatives trade, but sources do not state a position on markets under collective ownership.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the redistributive aim of the national program of struggle; not addressed directly.

basic-income.rationale: Zapatistas refuse government handouts as co-optation, but basic needs are demanded; adherents are split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: They oppose NAFTA but focus on peasants and land, not industrial tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from hostility to the state as an instrument of capital and preference for community control of production.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Communal land is preferred to either private or state holdings, but small peasant tenure is also accepted; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Sixth Declaration attacks wage exploitation but sets out no program to abolish money; Zapatista communities still use money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Anti-capitalist, so no wish to leave money to the market; abolition itself is not a Zapatista theme.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies fixing wages contradict the demand for autonomy from the state and from parties.

one-party-rule.rationale: The EZLN rejects vanguard rule and demands democracy; it declines to seek power and says it is not a party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Rejects hereditary rule; sovereignty resides in the people per Article 39 as cited in the First Declaration.

democracy-best.rationale: They demand democracy, yet define it as community assemblies and governing by obeying, and reject the current electoral system.

direct-votes.rationale: Major decisions go back to village communities through consultas, which is direct decision by the base.

workers-councils.rationale: Autonomous councils and assemblies of delegates resemble councils, but they are community-based rather than workplace-based.

right-to-secede.rationale: Independence was named among early demands, but the EZLN stresses autonomy within Mexico and never made secession a program.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rotating, recallable leaders and "the people command" deny any natural fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The EZLN launched an armed uprising and justified it, but now emphasizes a civil and peaceful path.

war-builds-character.rationale: The EZLN took up arms as a last resort and stresses peace, with no glorification of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Liberation theology shaped the movement but the EZLN keeps independence from religious authorities; no explicit statement.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The EZLN says it has no ties to religious authorities and bases law on community assemblies and the constitution's Article 39.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Anti-capitalist and opposed to privatization; justice is a communal service provided by autonomous bodies.

military-superiority.rationale: The EZLN views the army as an instrument of the dictatorship and is opposed to militarism.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement is indigenous but calls on all of Mexico's exploited and nonindigenous allies, rejecting ethnic exclusivity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marcos added a Marxist element but neozapatismo blends Maya tradition, liberation theology and autonomism, so adherents are split on this thesis.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Demands for land, work, housing and food for everyone ("everything for everyone") imply material equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous control of land and resources is a defining demand and practice of the movement.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The First Declaration traces oppression back 500 years; reparations are not addressed explicitly.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from internationalism of the exploited rather than unions based on religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The slogan "everything for everyone, nothing for us" and the Sixth Declaration reject self-interest as a moral guide.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Community obligation is strong in Zapatista communities, but they also emphasize rights, so this is split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Defense of land, forests and water and "No to the destruction of nature" signs express a view of nature as more than a resource.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from rejection of coercive state control; not addressed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: They oppose megaprojects and neoliberal destruction, but do not reject industrial civilization wholesale.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from the stress on rooted community decision making and rejection of capitalist disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a communitarian and ecological outlook.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Governing by obeying through assemblies of human delegates is the opposite of algorithmic rule.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The EZLN uses the internet for communication, but no stated position on encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: They look to indigenous tradition but demand radical change and autonomy, not restoration of a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Sixth Declaration argues for a clear anti-capitalist stance; pragmatism without ideology is not endorsed.

direct-action.rationale: Building autonomous government and rejecting electoral politics is direct action, though they also made demands on the state and ran a candidate in 2018.

means-match-ends.rationale: Governing by obeying and building autonomy from below within the struggle itself embodies this principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Zapatista communities are farming communities building production systems; no support for foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rotation of posts reduces specialization of rulers but not division of labor broadly.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Demands for food, health, housing for all fit need-based distribution; no explicit statement.

production-for-use.rationale: The Sixth Declaration describes capitalism as based on exploitation and builds alternatives for people's needs; cooperatives focus on subsistence.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Sixth Declaration states that capitalism is based on the exploitation of workers.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The EZLN rejects seizure of power and vanguard dictatorship; it says it does not seek power.

collective-farming.rationale: The EZLN communities run their own farming systems with indigenous control of land, which is largely collective in practice.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Sixth Declaration calls neoliberal globalization a war of conquest of the entire world, tying capitalism to war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Zapatistas are anti-capitalist and favor redistribution; taxation is not condemned as theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Community law bans alcohol and drugs, which exceeds a harm principle, but no explicit statement.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement claims collective rights for indigenous peoples and communal autonomy.

conscription.rationale: The EZLN opposes the state army; conscription is rejected as state coercion.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Zapatistas insist on voice through assemblies and the right to govern, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Neoliberal logic of governing as business is the target of the Sixth Declaration.

positive-liberty.rationale: Demands for land, work, health and education alongside freedom reflect that freedom needs material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Zapatistas use media strategically; they see capital and political class as holding power, not universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The movement arose against racism towards indigenous people; the genetic claim is rejected.

organic-representation.rationale: Delegates represent communities, but obey assemblies; corporate bodies are not used, and parties are rejected too.

total-state.rationale: They reject state control of life in favor of autonomy from below.

national-rebirth.rationale: They want radical transformation but no nationalist narrative of decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Anti-militarist and anti-imperialist; the EZLN rejects conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on assemblies and obeying the people, not oaths of loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: The uprising sought to end peasant servitude on large estates.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Zapatistas stress indigenous knowledge but no stated epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Marcos used mythopoetic story-telling and no stated stance on moral universals.

single-common-good.rationale: The Sixth Declaration acknowledges many struggles; they favor plural voices ("a world where many worlds fit") over one rational common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the sources I opened.

revive-national-language.rationale: They defend indigenous languages within Mexico but there is no stated policy on reviving a national language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Zapatistas favor democratic collective decision; large company governance is not directly discussed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Autonomous communities run their own education and oppose privatization.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Neoliberal fiscal orthodoxy is rejected, though deficits are not directly addressed.

economic-freedom.rationale: The claim ties political freedom to market freedom, which neoliberalism critics reject.

rule-by-example.rationale: Governing by obeying involves moral example, but laws and assemblies are also valued.

national-self-determination.rationale: They seek autonomy for indigenous peoples within Mexico rather than nation-states.

force-without-un.rationale: Anti-imperialist stance rejects unilateral force abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Maya tradition and liberation theology are part of the mix, but no statement on faith versus reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Solidarity with all the dispossessed rejects excluding immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from rights to food, health and work as claims on society and not as conditional benefits.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Sixth Declaration describes capital as exploiting workers; collaboration with employers is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: They call for solidarity among the exploited but not for a state-level front.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Women's Revolutionary Law and calls for women's participation reject fixed gender roles; Comandanta Esther: no longer time to be silent before men.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The movement is opposed to racial discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Sixth Declaration describes the political class and bad governments as serving capital, which resembles this view without a systematic theory.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Opposes privatization of oil and extractive megaprojects; expansion is rejected.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The movement defends cultural autonomy of indigenous peoples against assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: No source supports it; the Sixth Declaration views elites as exploiting the poor, not the replacement thesis.

proportional-representation.rationale: They reject parliamentary politics as such, so reform of electoral formulas is peripheral.

national-mission.rationale: Opposes exporting a government form; stresses autonomy and respect for each people.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Women's Law and the Sixth Declaration acknowledge lack of respect for women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Sixth Declaration targets the political class and the bad government, naming PRI, PAN and PRD for betraying the San Andres Accords.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic coercion contradicts the dignity demand.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The First Declaration demands justice and accuses the army of abuses; accountability follows.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The struggle is for dignity and equal rights for those excluded.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; the Sixth Declaration is internationalist, but its position on this theory is unstated.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The First Declaration traces dispossession to 500 years of conquest; settler states are not discussed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: They defend autonomous indigenous law, so single civil law for all is opposed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from religious freedom for communities; unaddressed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Peasant farm communities raise cattle; no such ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; autonomous schools are community controlled.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The EZLN rejects seizing state power and building a stronger state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The First Declaration cites Article 39: sovereignty resides in the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is not addressed; opposes export-driven neoliberalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts the dignity and rights demand.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: They initiated an armed uprising in 1994, but now stress peaceful struggle; pure non-initiation is not their position.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Zapatista ethic is mutual aid and solidarity.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from distrust of state powers; unaddressed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: "We fought to be free, not to change masters" fits freedom as non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: They want the military under civilians and delegates under assemblies, but not specifically checks among bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: The EZLN rejects vanguard leadership, saying peoples decide among themselves.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The movement is built around the exploited and dispossessed.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing is a demand, but not tenure.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Allies are workers' organizations; restrictions on strikes are opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: They attribute poverty to exploitation and neoliberal policy.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices are chosen by communities, not by lot, though rotation is valued.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: They suffered state repression and demand justice.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Food is a demand; price controls inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: The movement uses its own independent media and rejects party control.

party-commands-army.rationale: The EZLN military is separated from the autonomous governments.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from governing by obeying and the principle that authorities are delegates of the community; my sources do not document pay rules.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The EZLN rejects party politics and sees delegates as bound to communities, not to a party line; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Opposes supranational neoliberal structures; the EU is not addressed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: They reject presidential power and demand military subordination to civilian democratic authority.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Liberation theology under Bishop Ruiz favored grassroots church; bishops-led church is not endorsed.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clerics contradicts the demand that sovereignty reside in the people.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; the Sixth Declaration opposes war but there is no Leninist defeatist line.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The EZLN uses storytelling and culture as tools of struggle and opposes state control of life.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: "Not to change masters every six years" and rotation of posts oppose entrenched leaders.

recall-officials.rationale: Leaders are accountable and temporary and delegates are recallable by the communities.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing is a demand but rental is not mentioned.

people-in-arms.rationale: The EZLN is an armed force of the people, but separates itself from civil government and now emphasizes peaceful means.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Peasant culture is valued but there is no claim about moral health of rural life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Intellectuals and students are invited as allies; not endorsed.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: A demand for dignity and "a world where many worlds fit" assumes no culture is higher than another.

death-penalty.rationale: The EZLN struggle is for justice and life; the First Declaration's summary trials of the army are a war measure.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality is supported in autonomous education; sex education inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; autonomous schools teach community knowledge and Maya heritage mixed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; communities ban alcohol and drugs but no stated position here.

minority-language-support.rationale: Indigenous language and culture rights are central to the San Andres demands the EZLN champions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Community conformity and individual liberty both feature; no stated position.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Opposition to neoliberal globalization includes rejection of debt burdens on poor countries.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Independence is a demand together with land, work and anticapitalism; formal independence alone is insufficient.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Sixth Declaration calls for a new constitution built with the people.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Freedom and democracy are core demands, not deferrable.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Solidarity with the world's poor implies duty, but Zapatistas reject paternalist aid.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: They reject state electoral politics as such, so the head of state election method is peripheral.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: None of the Zapatista texts I opened concern territorial disputes between states, so adherents have no documented position and are split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Land and natural resources are held to serve the community, in contrast to privatization.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; neozapatismo is not tied to Soviet debates.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Opposition to megaprojects suggests precaution; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The sources I opened do not address annexation between states; no position is documented, so this is left neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: They reject state control of life; the church's role is community-based.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; the head of state function is outside their program.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The EZLN fights the state's army and argues peoples' right to self-governing.

region-keeps-system.rationale: They demand autonomy within Mexico for indigenous regions with their own justice and governance.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contradicts sovereignty of the people and rotation of rulers.

character-from-environment.rationale: Poverty and exclusion are explained by social conditions; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The First Declaration condemns illegitimate rulers and invokes constitutional popular sovereignty.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a concern; inferred from rooted ecological values.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rule by the many is the principle; mixed rule with elites is not.

leader-cult.rationale: The EZLN says it has no single leader and masks its spokespeople, and rejects changing masters.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court custody rules are not addressed in the Zapatista declarations or accounts of autonomy, so no position can be inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Zapatistas do not claim to build a socialist state, and none of the sources I opened discuss class struggle under socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land is a stated demand and the end of land reform in 1992 was a trigger of the uprising.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with the dispossessed.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Women's Law and Comandanta Esther demand women's freedom from subordination.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary unions between states are not discussed in the declarations; the movement has no documented view on currency design.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political unity of peoples by language family is not part of the Zapatista program, which concerns autonomy within Mexico and solidarity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Self-governing cultural, educational and political institutions within Mexico is precisely the autonomy model.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: They fight for equal rights within Mexico rather than founding a separate homeland.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marcos added a Marxist element but the movement draws on Maya tradition and theology; split.

ban-cartels.rationale: They oppose concentrations of capital but trust-busting is not their approach.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts of banks serve capital; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from distrust of the state.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Zapatistas call for more women in authority positions; Good Government councils declared women's participation a challenge.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: They defend local self-sufficiency but not imperial blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: They reject NAFTA wholesale rather than amend it with standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: The slogan "everything for everyone, nothing for us" and unpaid service ethic; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The EZLN's own uprising was an armed act but it says it does not seek to seize power and now rejects armed vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equality and rule by the people reject hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: School curricula centred on one's own civilization are not addressed, though autonomous schools stress community and Maya heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The First Declaration condemns 500 years of colonial domination.

patriotic-education.rationale: The EZLN uses a Mexican national flag but the movement stresses indigenous and international identities.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Active correction of exclusion is supported.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation and banking design are not discussed in the declarations I read, beyond general opposition to neoliberal finance.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Sixth Declaration treats capitalism as a system of exploitation and destruction to be replaced.

delink-world-market.rationale: They reject neoliberal integration but also seek international solidarity; they trade coffee abroad.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The Sixth Declaration calls on workers everywhere; this thesis is unaddressed.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The First Declaration is rooted in ending the exclusion of indigenous people, so a right to discriminate privately runs against its demand for dignity and justice.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: A new constitution recognizing the rights of the people is demanded.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from rejection of colonial-era dispossession.

elective-rulers.rationale: Local authorities are chosen by communities with rotation.

minority-veto.rationale: Decisions are taken by community consensus yet bind communities collectively; a single-member veto is not documented.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The First Declaration invokes the right to alter government by force under Article 39 against illegitimate rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Sixth Declaration rejects parliamentary politics, favoring communities.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed in the sources I opened; the ecological themes concern land, forests and water.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Solidarity from below, not charity from the privileged, is the model.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Active political participation and organization is central.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The Sixth Declaration criticizes media and neoliberalism; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Zapatista texts blame exploitation and the bad government but offer no theory of hegemony and consent, so the answer is neutral.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Sixth Declaration describes neoliberal globalization as plundering the peoples of the world.

party-own-road.rationale: The EZLN is independent from any party and rejects outside direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Zapatistas have long refused government aid, building autonomous services; solidarity donations accepted.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: They demand indigenous autonomy and rights within the whole of Mexico, not rule over non-indigenous people.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparison of fascism and communism is not addressed in the declarations I read, and Marxist and anarchist currents disagree on it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The First Declaration reflects a critical view of colonial history.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Priority on correcting women's subordination; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Women's Law stresses violence against women; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Zapatistas build their own governance based on indigenous tradition rather than copy Western institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The EZLN is firmly against the military's role in politics and separates its own forces from civil authority.

filial-duty.rationale: Obligations of adult children to parents are not addressed in the sources; community norms may favor it but nothing documents a position.

office-by-exam.rationale: Authorities are chosen and rotated by community, not by exam.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not addressed in the sources I opened, so adherents' position is left neutral.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Governing by obeying describes delegates bound by communities and removable.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal land held by use is consistent with indigenous communal tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Zapatistas reject parliamentary politics as practiced and do not discuss budget procedure, so no position is documented.

single-official-language.rationale: Indigenous language rights are a central demand.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The Sixth Declaration defends national resources against privatization to foreigners, but foreign ownership of land is not directly addressed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from "more respect for humanity than for money".

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Sixth Declaration offers material support to some peoples, but this concerns state arming; rejected.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed in my sources; the EZLN focuses on autonomy within Mexico, not national reunification.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Sixth Declaration describes capitalists and neoliberal governments as working together against the people, so adherents see corporate power over government as a central ill.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: the movement depends on international solidarity networks and would see such restrictions as a tool against civil society.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on women's autonomy and on community rather than state direction of family life; not addressed directly.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the centrality of communal land held by those who live and work on it, and from the demand for land.

job-guarantee.rationale: Work is among the First Declaration's listed demands, so a guaranteed job fits, though adherents would favour community rather than state provision.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: Zapatistas reject the electoral democracy of the Mexican state and of neoliberal globalization, and do not treat exporting it as a path to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The First Declaration declares war on an illegitimate government and the movement runs its own autonomous authorities, implying no automatic duty to obey state law.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from opposition to imperial and neoliberal domination, though the movement is also internationalist in its solidarity.

industrial-unions.rationale: Unions are not a main Zapatista subject; the Sixth Declaration seeks workers' alliances without preferring a union form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: the movement defends indigenous peoples against racism and builds an inclusive 'world where many worlds fit', so it rejects scapegoating minorities.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; communities regulate family life by custom and adherents are not documented as favouring abolition or defending state marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from governing by obeying: Good Government assemblies and consultas rely on open accountability to communities.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from opposition to NAFTA and neoliberalism and from the emphasis on community self-sufficiency and autonomy.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement rejects parties but builds permanent assemblies, councils and a federation of autonomous municipalities, so it does not favour only small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Split: the First Declaration invokes the national constitution's Article 39, yet the movement rejects the Mexican state and trade treaties that override local rights.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred: the movement speaks for a plural, multi-ethnic Mexican people and rejects religion as the basis of political community.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the EZLN's anti-imperialism and its demand for dignity among peoples; ritual submission to a leading power is contrary to it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Zapatista autonomy rests on solidarity: Good Government Councils redistribute resources among communities, and the Declarations call for sharing according to need.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from communal land tenure and anti-capitalism; the EZLN's collective land claims coexist with personal belongings, which are not at issue.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: the EZLN is hostile to Cold War blocs and state power, and refuses coexistence-or-defeat framings between states.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from opposition to privatisation and the preference for community-run health and education in the autonomous municipalities.

religion-illusion.rationale: The EZLN rooted itself in liberation theology and Maya tradition and respects religious belief, rather than treating it as an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Sixth Declaration describes capitalism as plunder and exploitation, the central object of the EZLN's struggle.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Sixth Declaration ties exploitation and women's subordination to capitalism, and the EZLN's Women's Revolutionary Law pairs gender equality with its wider program.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from community-run services and collective self-government, which suggest shared care work; not documented directly.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of indigenous languages alongside Spanish, which is also the language of its communiques.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: the EZLN's negotiations centred on government honouring the San Andres Accords, so agreements with indigenous peoples should bind the state.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The autonomous municipalities hold land and goods in common and govern by assembly, which is the Zapatista model of society.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the demand for indigenous land and autonomy and the rejection of state colonisation of indigenous regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Sixth Declaration rejects both neoliberal capitalism and old authoritarian state socialism in favour of a new path from below.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Land and indigenous territorial rights are central to the movement, and the First Declaration lists land among its demands.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; adherents reject denial of documented fact, inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not a stated position; the movement stresses dignity and the rights of the excluded, so adherents would oppose criminalising it, though communities vary.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Governing by obeying and community assemblies rest on open pluralism and consultation, not on suppressing dissent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The movement is secular in its politics and mixes religious traditions, so civil punishment of religion is inferred as opposed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement opposes neoliberalism and colonial domination of indigenous peoples, so territories governed for another's benefit are rejected.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: They fight bad government for popular sovereignty, not religious law, so this basis for removal is not theirs; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Governing by obeying, community assemblies, consultations and rotation of leaders are core practice.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The Sixth Declaration links exploitation of workers, indigenous people and women under capitalism; inferred this extends to overlapping oppression.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; the movement defends the excluded and has spoken against discrimination, inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents would be split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Zapatistas identify with the left, 'from below and to the left', in the Sixth Declaration, rather than transcending the divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anti-capitalism with Marxist elements sees capital exploiting workers, though alienation per se is not their own language.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is pluralist, so adherents would not accept this claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Article 39 popular sovereignty in the First Declaration places authority in the people, not God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The movement respects religious and indigenous practice and would not ban its display; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the movement's support for women's rights and anti-corporate stance.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement rejects both neoliberal capitalism and state-run solutions, so a market with a social net is not its aim; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The EZLN is itself an armed force, though it wants the state's army defeated and a peaceful autonomous order; adherents are split.

rich-first.rationale: The movement opposes neoliberal trickle-down logic and demands equality and dignity for all now.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The movement is anti-imperialist and anti-NAFTA, so stays away from great-power blocs; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Zapatismo rests on governing by obeying and on rotating community-chosen authorities, which excludes inherited office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from the Zapatista focus on cooperatives and autonomous community economies in opposition to profit-driven capitalism.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The movement opposes neoliberal capitalism and the foreign-imposed economic order, and its declarations demand national self-determination.

property-franchise.rationale: Zapatista governance runs by community assemblies open to all members, with no wealth test.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Zapatista women shaped the movement and its Revolutionary Women's Law, and the movement ties exploitation of people to that of the land, though it frames them in its own terms.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-capitalist analysis and its Marxist influences, which see markets as hiding human relations.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the movement's critique of how capital and the state control information, and from its building of its own media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The movement rejects state law yet runs its own community justice, case by case through councils, so adherents are split on this wording.

racial-franchise.rationale: The EZLN is indigenous-led but demands justice for all and speaks for the excluded of every kind, rejecting racism.

online-participation.rationale: Zapatista decisions are made in face-to-face assemblies, though the movement uses the internet widely for communication and solidarity.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from Good Government Councils that rotate and account to the communities for their work.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from the movement's inclusive stance; its communities include several faiths and it rejects discrimination.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of discrimination and its call for solidarity among the excluded.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Zapatistas stress governing by obeying, rotating posts and community assemblies, which suggests sympathy for deliberation by ordinary people, though lot selection is not their method; inferred from the Sixth Declaration and the Good Government Councils.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Zapatismo blends Maya tradition with liberation theology and is critical of hierarchical church authority, so it favours reading doctrine in light of present conditions; inferred, not stated as a position.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Zapatismo opposes neoliberal capitalism and demands land and a fair share for the dispossessed, implying concentrated wealth threatens self-government.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Sixth Declaration lists homosexuals among the excluded the movement stands with; open service is an inference, and the EZLN is itself an army, hence low confidence.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Zapatismo draws on Maya tradition and liberation theology and does not seek to impose unbelief; inferred from its respect for community belief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Autonomous communities handle justice through community councils and without conventional prisons, though abolition is not an explicit demand; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Zapatismo seeks indigenous autonomy rather than guaranteed shares of state executive power, and it refuses state power altogether; inferred as neutral.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Zapatismo holds that communities should organise social provision themselves but also demands state obligations to indigenous people; mixed, inferred slightly against charity framing.

term-limits.rationale: Governing by obeying includes rotating posts that communities hand out and revoke, which favours short tenure.

vote-delegation.rationale: Zapatista autonomy relies on direct assembly participation and recallable posts rather than proxy voting; delegation of a vote by topic is inferred to be marginal.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Zapatismo does not address extinction risk as a policy priority; adherents split.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Zapatismo promotes women's participation in leadership and the Women's Revolutionary Law; religious offices are an inference.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Women's Revolutionary Law gives women equal rights and a say in decisions, including in the family; shared marital authority fits this.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the Sixth Declaration's border-crossing solidarity with the world's exploited; residents' voting is not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the First Declaration's demands for housing and its anti-neoliberal stance; rent caps are not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from opposition to neoliberal privatisation of knowledge and seeds and community-held autonomy; not stated directly.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from its refusal to seize state power and its civilian community self-government; national-service youth drill is not discussed.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the anti-war, anti-capitalist outlook of the Sixth Declaration; the issue is not addressed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the First Declaration's national-sovereignty and anti-imperial framing; foreign bases are not discussed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from adherents' framing of the repression of indigenous peoples; formal recognition by governments is not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Sixth Declaration targets capitalism's exploitation of workers and peasants, which implies rewarding work over ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The First Declaration invokes a right to take up arms against oppression, and the EZLN is an armed force, so absolute pacifism is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on indigenous peoples' autonomy over a unified Mexican nation story; not stated directly.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred only; autonomy-practice sources give no position on whether sex itself is constructed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Zapatista women's organising is documented, but no position on a fixed category of 'women' is stated; inferred as split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The EZLN commemorates its fallen but is non-statist and not nationalist; honouring them as martyrs and saints is inferred, not stated.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from its framing of struggle as dignity, land and autonomy against neoliberalism, not a cosmic good-versus-evil contest.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is not diaspora-oriented, so the answer is left neutral.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from building autonomous communities from below instead of seizing state power.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the movement's blend of Maya tradition and liberation theology; the statement is not discussed directly.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred; liberation-theology and Maya elements are present but no position on judging texts by women's humanity is documented.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The First Declaration demands justice for indigenous people, a minority in Mexico, so entrenching majority control of the economy is opposed.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from indigenous peoples' autonomous municipalities and regions; merging administrative regions is not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: The Sixth Declaration rejects parties and the state's capture of popular organisations, so unions answering to their members fits; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Good Government councils and governing by obeying put power in communities and assemblies, and the EZLN refuses to seize the state, so socialism without workers' and peasants' own power is rejected.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Autonomous municipalities run their own health, education and services under community control, so basic local services stay in public (communal) hands.

second-chamber.rationale: Power flows from local assemblies upward through councils, and a further layer of institutions above the elected body runs against that; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Land and its use are held communally by indigenous communities, which fits community ownership; the exact form of productive property is an inference.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Good Government Councils coordinate autonomous municipalities while delegates obey assemblies, which is close to the statement's description.

family-wage.rationale: The Sixth Declaration demands decent work, pay and living conditions against neoliberalism; family wages are inferred from that.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; neoliberal critiques of regulators and distrust of pharmaceutical firms point both ways.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed, and the movement's concern is basic health access for poor communities, so no clear stance.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; distrust of state control is balanced by hostility to financial capital.

online-anonymity.rationale: The EZLN's fighters wear masks to hide individual identity and speak collectively, so anonymity under pseudonyms is natural to them; online use is inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Governing by obeying and the demand for dignity make officials servants of communities and persons, so the person is not a means for the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement blends Maya tradition and liberation theology, so people's spiritual and material needs are both recognised.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: They demand autonomy for indigenous peoples and reject an all-powerful central state, so regional self-rule revocable by the national legislature is not accepted.

gm-crops.rationale: Their opposition to neoliberal agribusiness and defence of indigenous maize farming suggests wariness of genetically engineered crops; inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is rural and indigenous and makes no claim about urban density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The First Declaration speaks for indigenous peoples organised as such, though this is ethnic and cultural rather than racial in the usual sense.

racial-pride.rationale: The First Declaration and later texts affirm indigenous dignity and pride against centuries of contempt.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The uprising is framed as defence of peoples against an oppressive army and state, but the EZLN also declared war, so this is an inference.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The EZLN speaks for many indigenous peoples with different languages inside Mexico and, in the Sixth Declaration, for a plural nation of struggles; it does not tie nationhood to a single language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Zapatismo rests on assemblies of all community members and rejects party electoral politics; separate electorates for religious communities are not part of that model, an inference.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The EZLN blames the Mexican government and neoliberal capital, and rejects nationalism, stressing struggle against the bad government rather than foreign plots to break up the country.

free-public-college.rationale: The First Declaration demands education for all and the autonomous municipalities run their own schools, so adherents want education guaranteed without charge, though through community provision.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Zapatistas oppose treating nature and life as commodities and reject market mechanisms, so a tax on pollution as the main tool is inferred as unwelcome.

future-generations.rationale: Zapatismo draws on Maya ideas of land as mother and a commitment to the children and the world to come, and its declarations speak of struggling for future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The EZLN's Revolutionary Women's Law and strong female presence push for women's participation, but the sources do not claim women carry distinct values, so this is inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: The EZLN took up arms as a last resort and now stresses civil, peaceful organising, so it would favour reducing armaments, though it kept its own forces; an inference.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Zapatismo stresses governing by obeying and public assemblies, so secret international agreements that bypass peoples are inferred as objectionable.

capital-controls.rationale: The EZLN attacks global finance and neoliberal free trade, but it rejects seizing state power, so it would not simply entrust the state with controlling capital; adherents' view is unclear.

missingStatements.text: Political leaders should govern by obeying the decisions of the communities they serve.
missingStatements.rationale: Mandar obedeciendo is the core Zapatista principle of authority, documented in the autonomous governance structure.

missingStatements.text: Free-trade agreements that open markets to foreign capital are an attack on peasant and indigenous peoples.
missingStatements.rationale: The uprising began on the day NAFTA took effect, and the EZLN holds it worsens inequality.

missingStatements.text: Communities should be able to run their own schools, health care and justice systems without state control.
missingStatements.rationale: Autonomous municipalities provide justice, health and education and refuse permission-seeking from the state.

notes: The EZLN's stance is contested between anarchist, Marxist and indigenous readings; it also changed over time from armed uprising (1994) to civil, non-electoral struggle (2005), a 2018 candidate, and 2023 reorganization into local autonomous governments.
